text: Every endpoint needs an unauthenticated request expecting 401 and an authenticated request from an account without the right expecting 403.
When an operation cascades to related records, assert the state of those related records afterwards, not only the primary resource.
A resource with a lifecycle needs one case per illegal transition, not a single representative one.
Anything that creates a record or grants access needs a repeated-request case proving the second call is either idempotent or rejected.
Reads by identifier need a case where the record exists but belongs to somebody else, expecting the not-found response rather than the forbidden one, so existence is not disclosed.
Anything that issues a credential needs an expiry case and a replay case that presents the same credential twice.
When a credential is replaced or withdrawn, prove the previous one stops working, not only that the new one starts.
Verify entitlement changes against a session that was already open, not only against a fresh sign-in.
Idle and absolute limits are separate cases, and renewal must be shown unable to extend past the absolute one.
Enrolment is incomplete without the fallback codes: one authenticates once, and the same one is refused on reuse.
Every form needs a case for the message shown against the offending field, not only for the failed submission as a whole.
Wherever the browser rejects input before sending it, add a case that posts the same payload directly to the server.
Anywhere a document can be attached, cover an oversized one, one whose declared type does not match its contents, and an empty one.
Postal formats differ by country, so include a destination whose format is not the default one.
Where a value must be unique, include two simultaneous submissions carrying the same value.
Batch input needs a partial-failure case: some entries rejected, the remainder committed, and the report identifying which line failed.
Every migration needs a reversal case exercised against records written after it ran.
Cover the rows that do not fit the expected shape: single-token values, blanks, and rows that already look converted.
Tightening a column to reject empties needs one case proving nothing is left empty and one for records written while the fill is still in progress.
Numeric conversions need the largest and smallest stored values and a value that does not divide evenly, so rounding direction is pinned down.
Clock shifts produce local readings that occur twice and readings that never occur; each needs its own case.
When records are collapsed into one, prove that references held elsewhere resolve to the survivor.
Actions that change who can reach what must assert that a trail entry was written naming the account that acted.
Cases carry an explicit priority and the highest-priority ones are listed first.
